rationale: Repair of trial-8469963975, which reached the communication floor (33.12 ms vs the 53.63 ms baseline) but was rejected solely on the step_ms constraint: 127.07 ms median vs the 120.90 ms limit (1.05x 115.14), because it fused all 497,759,232 bytes into one barrier-aligned allreduce issued only after backward completed, plus pack/cuda-sync/unpack on the critical path, giving up the reducer's overlap (baseline: the 13-bucket collective pipeline runs +139.3->+185.0 ms while the 4th microbatch's backward runs ~+135->+168.4 ms, only ~16.5 ms exposed). This candidate replaces project.invoke (group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb, the boundary the previous trial proved coherent) with the parent's unchanged step - zero_grad, four microbatches with no_sync on the first three, final synchronized backward, SGD step, torch.cuda.synchronize - plus a gradient-synchronization policy installed once per process on the existing DDP wrapper via model.register_comm_hook. The comm hook keeps the baseline's progressive launch schedule: it fires exactly when each 25 MiB bucket becomes final during the final microbatch's backward and flushes ready buckets in small fused chunks (one ProcessGroupNCCL grouped allreduce over the chunk's bucket buffers, in place on the same fp32 storage, gradient_as_bucket_view preserved, no packing and no scratch). The arithmetic is the default reducer's: divide by world_size then SUM, so for world_size 2 the result is bitwise identical to the baseline per element (division by 2 is an exact power-of-two scaling, so fl(a/2+b/2) == fl((a+b)/2), and grouping only changes kernel scheduling, never per-element adds). The skew that inflates the objective - measured 3.0-3.7 ms CPU submit spread per collective, rank 0's kernels 2.4-5.4 ms vs rank 1's 1.9 ms wire (current execution_timeline-1221e205) - is absorbed CPU-side: one gloo control-group barrier (plus local stream drain) immediately before the synchronized backward, and one gloo barrier before each chunk submission. Gloo barriers emit no NCCL kernels, so they do not enter the kernel-duration metric; their CPU wait lands on the early rank, whose wall was already paced by the late rank in the baseline. Expected, to be tested on the leased worker: diagnostic.max_rank_nccl_kernel_sum_ms drops from 53.63 ms to ~34-38 ms (floor ~33.4 ms = measured wire cost: 12x ~1.9 ms + 10.6 ms; residual = post-alignment jitter) while step_ms stays near the ~115 ms baseline: the late rank gains only ~2-5 barrier intrinsics (~0.1-0.3 ms each), Python hook dispatch across 13 hook calls, and ~1 ms of div work that the C++ reducer also performed, with ~29 ms of the ~34 ms wire still hidden under the remaining backward compute. Previous feedback changes this attempt in three concrete ways: (1) communication is re-overlapped with the final backward instead of serialized after it; (2) alignment happens before NCCL submission (CPU wait) instead of inside NCCL kernels (device spin counted by the metric); (3) no pack/sync/unpack is placed on the critical path because the grouped allreduce operates in place on the bucket views. The two observed DDP reducer allreduce sites (d0938de87369efd500322679, 12x 28,351,488 B; b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b, 1x 157,541,376 B) are eliminated: their consumer is gradient synchronization itself, and p.grad now receives bitwise-identical synchronized values from the hook policy before optimizer.step() and every harness check (exact cross-rank equality via identical NCCL grouping on both ranks, serial-reference gradient/parameter comparisons on identical values, negative control unchanged). State lifecycle is preserved: run_index increment, optimizer state, reset()/load_state_dict compatibility (the policy lives on the DDP wrapper object and survives resets), no parameter transformation, no CUDA Graph capture, no cached outputs, and the workload executes on current inputs every invocation on both ranks. Fallbacks are explicit: unsupported state (non-CUDA, world_size 1, no DDP, non-NCCL default backend, missing/non-gloo control group, non-fp32 CUDA params) routes to the parent with the 'invoke:unsupported-state:parent-fallback' label; a register_comm_hook failure routes to the parent with 'invoke:comm-hook-setup-failed:parent-fallback'; runtime collective failures propagate through the per-bucket futures as exceptions so DDP fails fast instead of hanging. The flush granularity (buckets_per_flush) and per-chunk barrier mode (flush_alignment) are tunable so the coordinator can trade barrier count against residual kernel wait; the pre-backward alignment and the progressive schedule are fixed parts of the policy.

setup_work.build: No GPU work and no parameter transformation at build(): only validates the observed project.invoke target spec (kind 'project', target 'project.invoke') and the parent reference, then installs the replacement callable.
setup_work.first_invocation: Lazily installs the policy once per process at the first invoke: model.register_comm_hook on the existing DDP wrapper (state['model']). DDP's register path fires one 1-element async flag allreduce on the NCCL default group, matched on both ranks inside the first warmup invocation; no buffers are allocated, no weights are packed or copied, and the hook is stored on the DDP object so later invocations reuse it.
setup_work.per_invocation: The step runs the parent's exact sequence. Immediately before the final microbatch's forward/backward it drains the local default stream and joins one gloo control-group barrier. During the synchronized backward the comm hook fires per ready bucket, divides pending bucket buffers by world_size in place (fused _foreach_div_), optionally joins one gloo barrier per flush, and issues one grouped NCCL SUM allreduce over the chunk's bucket buffers in place; deferred per-bucket futures resolve when their chunk's work completes. No packing copies and no scratch memory are added; on-device traffic is the same gradient bytes as the baseline plus one extra element-wise pass over each buffer (the division the C++ reducer also performs).
setup_work.memory: No new CUDA allocations: the policy operates in place on the existing gradient bucket storage (gradient_as_bucket_view), so per-run peak_allocated_bytes and reserved memory are unchanged from the baseline warm-model lifecycle apart from the one-element flag tensor DDP itself allocates at hook registration.

quality_risks: Exact cross-rank gradient equality (atol=0, rtol=0) relies on both ranks grouping buckets identically: DDP invokes the hook in the same bucket-readiness order on every rank (the same invariant the baseline's stream-ordered NCCL allreduces depend on), and each chunk is one NCCL SUM whose inputs are pre-divided by world_size, giving values bitwise identical to the baseline per element for world_size 2.

The deferred per-bucket futures gate DDP's backward completion on the final flush; bucket.is_last() triggers that flush, and any collective or barrier error is propagated by setting exceptions on all outstanding futures so the step fails fast rather than hanging (worker timeout as the backstop).

Gloo barriers inside the timed step are CPU-only (no NCCL kernels) but their latency sits on the critical path of the late rank (~0.1-0.3 ms each, ~2-5 per step depending on buckets_per_flush); the step_ms constraint has ~5.8 ms of headroom and the flush_alignment/buckets_per_flush parameters let the coordinator reduce alignment points if the measured wall time approaches the limit.

The pre-backward local stream drain trades a small serial wait (tail of the third microbatch's backward) on both ranks for GPU-queue alignment; it costs wall time but no NCCL kernel time, and the metric is unaffected by gloo barrier CPU waits.

The policy must stay active identically on both ranks: the supported-state predicate checks only rank-symmetric state (device type, world size, DDP/NCCL presence, fp32 CUDA parameters, gloo control group), so a fallback on one rank implies the same fallback on the other; no collective is issued on a fallback path.

One flaky 385.8 ms clean sample appeared in the previous trial; this policy adds lockstep barriers rather than removing them, and acceptance is decided by medians over the 3 diagnostic invocations and 5 clean repeats, not single samples.

params.name: buckets_per_flush
params.description: Number of ready 25 MiB DDP gradient buckets (~7,087,872 fp32 elements each) accumulated before one fused NCCL allreduce flush during the final microbatch's backward; the last bucket always flushes everything pending. Smaller values align finer (less residual kernel wait) with more barrier points; larger values issue fewer, larger grouped collectives with less barrier latency on the pacing rank. Chunk fusion changes only kernel scheduling, never per-element arithmetic.

params.name: flush_alignment
params.description: Whether each flush joins a gloo control-group barrier (CPU-side rank alignment, emits no NCCL kernels) before submitting its grouped allreduce. 'none' keeps only the pre-backward alignment; 'barrier' re-aligns before every chunk to suppress residual in-kernel wait.
